`/work/combi_brualdi_ch11_5.lean` now compiles with no errors, and the `sorry` is replaced by a full proof. Lean still prints a deprecation warning for `push_neg`, which I left as is. I didn't change the imports or the theorem statement.

The proof is by contradiction with the pigeonhole principle. Assume all `n` vertices have different degrees. Then:

- **Some vertex has degree 0:** every other vertex `v` has no edge to it. So `v`'s neighbours lie among the `n - 2` vertices other than `v` and that one. Every degree is therefore in `{0, …, n-2}`, which has only `n - 1` values.
- **No vertex has degree 0:** every degree is at least 1 and at most `n - 1`. So all degrees lie in `{1, …, n-1}`, which again has only `n - 1` values.

Either way, `n` vertices map into a set of size `n - 1`, so two of them share a degree.
